title: Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2022
short_title: Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would align specified Commonwealth superannuation arrangements with general fund choice rules, including use of an existing fund linked to a new employee.
It would allow alternative default funds when existing defaults could no longer accept new members after failing annual performance tests in two consecutive years.
New parliamentarians and relevant judges could receive contributions into an existing linked fund when they made no choice, with changes beginning after royal assent.
changes: The Finance Minister would prescribe default fund selection methods through instruments that Parliament could disallow.
Default fund selection would have to consider fees, costs and investment returns, through assessment or publicly available rankings.
Employer contribution rates for an alternative public service default fund could not fall below the corresponding public service scheme rate.
summary.affected: New parliamentarians, public service employees, judges of the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia (Division 2), Commonwealth employers and superannuation funds would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The Public Sector Superannuation Legislation Amendment Bill 2022 makes consequential amendments to the Parliamentary Superannuation Act 2004, the Superannuation Act 2005, and the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia Act 2021 to apply the Your Future, Your Super reforms to Commonwealth public sector superannuation, including stapling super accounts to members when they change jobs and establishing new default fund arrangements if a fund fails the annual performance test for two consecutive years.
